Why now

The rules changed on September 21, 2026

Ontario's Landlord and Tenant Board brought in legislative and form changes this fall. If your templates predate them, they may already be out of date.

SEPT 21, 2026

New N4, shorter clock

Notices given on or after September 21 must be on the new N4 (2026/09) form, and the notice period dropped from 14 days to 7. An N4 on the old form, or with the old timeline, can fail.

SEPT 21, 2026

Eleven forms replaced at once

The N4, N5, N6, N8, N12, N13, L1, L2, L9, L10 and T5 were all replaced on September 21 — and "persistent late payment" is now defined as rent more than 7 days late on at least 3 occasions in any 6-month period.

SEPT 21, 2026

N12 compensation change

For an N12 given on or after September 21 with a termination date at least 120 days out, at the end of a rental period or fixed term, the one month's rent compensation may no longer be owed. Shorter N12s — and a purchaser's own-use N12 — still need it.

NOV 30, 2026

Old forms stop being accepted

After November 30, 2026, the previous versions of those forms will no longer be accepted at all. A stale form after that date can sink a notice or an application outright.

Details from the Landlord and Tenant Board's operational update on the September 21, 2026 changes — read it on Tribunals Ontario. A checkup flags where these changes touch your documents; it isn't a substitute for legal advice on your situation.

How it works

Three steps, about 30 minutes

1

Get in touch

Email thepaperworkcheckup@gmail.com with the basics — who you are, which document, and the date or deadline you're working toward. Send a photo or scan of the document if you have one.

2

Get your review

Your document is checked for completeness, correct dates and deadlines, and whether it's on the current form — the same checks shown in the report above.

3

Work from the summary

You receive a short written summary with a missing-items list and suggested next steps, so you know exactly what to fix before anything is filed or served.

For landlords

  • Notices that hold up — N4s, N12s and other notices checked for the current form and correct dates before you serve them.
  • Filing packages in order — L1 and L2 applications reviewed together with their supporting documents.
  • Deadlines you won't miss — members get a hand keeping track of service, filing and hearing dates.

For tenants

  • Check a notice you received — is it on the current form? Is the termination date counted correctly? Was it given in time?
  • Know your dates — response and hearing deadlines laid out plainly, so nothing slips past.
  • Your own filings, organized — applications like the T5 reviewed for completeness before you submit them.

Questions

Good to know

Is this legal advice?+

No. PaperCheck is administrative and organizational help: checking forms for completeness, correct dates and current versions, and keeping deadlines organized. It is not legal advice and not representation at the Landlord and Tenant Board. For legal questions about your situation, speak to a licensed paralegal or lawyer.

Who is it for?+

Landlords and tenants anywhere in Ontario — small landlords with a unit or two, and tenants who've received a notice and want it checked. Everything is done remotely, by message and email.

What can I send for a checkup?+

One document per checkup: a lease, a notice (such as an N4 or N12), or an LTB filing package (such as an L1 or L2). Photos or scans are fine — you'll get a written summary of what's complete, what's missing, and the suggested next steps.

Is the first checkup really free?+

Yes — when you sign up, your first checkup is free: one document reviewed, with the full written summary. After that, checkups are part of the monthly membership — priced by how many units you have: up to 10 units is $59/month, 11–25 units is $99/month, and 26 or more units is $149/month.

Can I cancel my membership, or get a refund?+

Membership payments are not refundable once a month's payment has been made. To cancel, let us know at least 30 days before your next payment date. Your membership stays active to the end of that notice period, and no further payments are taken after it.

What changed at the LTB in September 2026?+

On September 21, 2026 the Board replaced its main forms (including the N4, N12, L1 and T5), shortened the N4 notice period from 14 days to 7, and changed the N12 compensation rule. Previous form versions stop being accepted after November 30, 2026. The full details are in the LTB's operational update on Tribunals Ontario.
